analysis.title: Weekly Viewpoint: Risk-Off Sentiment Pushes S&P Into a Technical Correction
key_insights: Week ending Nov. 20: Dow -8.0%, S&P 500 -8.6%, Nasdaq -10.0%. All 11 S&P sectors fell, with tech -12.2%, communication services -9.4% and materials -7.9%.
S&P 500 extended its losing streak to seven sessions and entered a technical correction, defined as a 10% pullback from its all-time high. The selloff was global.
AI trade trepidation persisted despite strong Nvidia results and guidance and a successful Anthropic public offering, which did not renew sector optimism.
Added pressure came from rising risk of US strikes on Iran and the growing risk of hacks and system outages.
Fedspeak leaned hawkish. Waller said the Fed should raise 50bp in December if it will not signal a more aggressive path, citing worry that 3% inflation becomes the new norm.
Goolsbee said he would consider all options in December, including a larger than usual hike. Musalem backed multiple hikes. Williams dismissed the need for an outsized hike.
Jefferson, Goolsbee and Kashkari linked the AI buildout to inflation pressure, risk of overheating and concentration risk if returns disappoint.
Oct. 27-28 FOMC minutes: nearly all officials saw rate increases likely in coming months. Two said more than 25bp could be warranted in December if inflation data are unfavorable.
Q3 earnings: 468 S&P 500 companies reported, over 84% beat, and aggregate earnings are up just over 32% YoY versus roughly 25% projected at end of September.
Full-year S&P 500 earnings growth is expected at 30.4% for 2026, 20.4% for 2027 and 16.4% for 2028.
Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 203,000 versus the 198,000 consensus. October retail sales rose 0.2% after 0.8% in September.
Week ahead: October PCE, personal income and spending, durable goods and new home sales on Wednesday, plus the Beige Book. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and at 1 p.m. ET Friday.

sector_views.rationale: Weakest sector at -12.2% for the week amid AI trade concerns. This is a description of performance, not an explicit rating.
Posted the biggest Q3 earnings upside surprises.
Strongest YoY Q3 earnings growth, followed by technology and industrials.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 reported results through Nov. 20: 468 companies, over 84% beat expectations, aggregate earnings up just over 32% YoY (reported), versus roughly 25% projected at end of September.
Nine of 11 sectors beat expectations. Healthcare and utilities had the biggest upside surprises. All 11 posted YoY gains, led by energy, technology and industrials.
Full-year S&P 500 earnings growth expectations (forecast): 30.4% in 2026, 20.4% in 2027, 16.4% in 2028.
Upcoming reporters this week (dozen S&P members): Dell Technologies, Analog Devices, Workday and Deere.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly above the 198,000 consensus but well below 222,000 a year earlier, so the labor market remains tight.
Actual print was modestly above the estimate.
Moderation as big ticket items like cars pulled back, with resilient demand elsewhere.
Key data focus this week given hawkish Fed rhetoric and a possible December hike.
Possible larger than 25bp hike keeps rate risk elevated for equities.
